extracted.intended_audience: earth scientists and researchers considering preprint deposition; general readers researching preprint servers
extracted.subtask_description: Information and practical criteria about EarthArXiv as a preprint server: what it accepts, what services it provides (DOIs, hosting), its scope and governance, and its role relative to peer-reviewed journals. Useful for authors deciding where/how to deposit earth-science preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of content / disciplines accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: EarthArXiv publishes pre- and postprints from all subdomains of Earth science and related domains of planetary science, including geochemistry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended submissions cover the full range of Earth science subdomains and related planetary science areas; authors from these fields may deposit preprints and postprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint definition and role relative to journals
rubrics_metrics.description: These publications are versions of scholarly papers that precede publication in peer-reviewed scientific journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EarthArXiv hosts versions of manuscripts prior to journal peer review/publication; authors should understand deposits are versions that precede journal publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: EarthArXiv is not a journal / no scientific quality evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: EarthArXiv is not itself a journal and does not evaluate the scientific quality of a paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform provides hosting and dissemination but does not perform peer review or formal scientific quality assessments; authors remain responsible for vetting content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigns DOIs for provenance and citability
rubrics_metrics.description: The EarthArXiv platform assigns each submission a Digital Object Identifier (DOI), therefore assigning provenance and making it citable in other scholarly works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions receive persistent identifiers enabling citation and provenance tracking—useful when citing or sharing preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content license: Creative Commons
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are released under Creative Commons licensing consistent with an open-access mission; authors should be aware of licensing implications for reuse and sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission types: preprints and postprints
rubrics_metrics.description: EarthArXiv publishes articles that are preprints and postprints (versions before and/or after journal publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may deposit both initial preprint versions and postprint versions; check EarthArXiv policy/platform for any versioning recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform services / technical infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Center for Open Science (COS) / California Digital Library provided technical infrastructure such as storage space, DOI generation, and web hosting (EarthArXiv later moved hosting to the California Digital Library and Janeway).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The repository provides technical services (hosting, DOI minting, platform) but community volunteers handle governance; platform choices affect discoverability and persistence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community and governance model
rubrics_metrics.description: EarthArXiv is a volunteer community devoted to open scholarly communication and uses shared governance (initially a working cluster and now maintained by the EarthArXiv Advisory Council).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The server's policies and operations are community-driven; participation, promotion, or policy changes may involve volunteers and advisory structures rather than a commercial editorial board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: promote open access and share resources
rubrics_metrics.description: EarthArXiv's mission is to promote open access, share open access and preprint resources, and participate in shared governance of the preprint server and its policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and community members should align submissions and contributions with the service's open-access and community-governance ethos.
